summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, severe aortic stenosis, and immune thrombocytopenic purpura was admitted with septic shock secondary to methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bursitis of the left elbow. She developed cardiogenic shock, NSTEMI, and vasopressor-induced lower extremity ischemia. Despite aggressive management including balloon valvuloplasty and broad-spectrum antibiotics, her hemodynamics deteriorated. A family meeting led to a decision for comfort-focused care. Pressors were withdrawn, a morphine drip was initiated, and she died peacefully. The hospital course was complicated by delirium, coagulopathy, and inability to effectively dialyze due to instability.
